page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core with 2 threads per core, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include any bundled local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor includes advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which support specialized vector and matrix operations.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core execution is moderate, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1640.0 and stress-ng single-core CPU performance reaching 1554.59, both placing in the average tier. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations show significant constraints. The Geekbench multi-core score of 2036.0 and the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 1600.79 fall into the weak and poor categories, respectively. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read-only large block bandwidth at 15.05 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 9.22 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10% of tested systems.

The primary tradeoff of the n4-highmem-2 is its high memory allocation relative to its limited processing power. While the 16.0 GB RAM capacity supports memory-bound workloads, the 2 vCPU limit restricts parallel processing, as evidenced by poor scores in multi-threaded tasks like software compilation and database operations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides a low-cost entry point for applications requiring more memory than standard general-purpose instances without the expense of scaling up vCPU counts. It is suited for lightweight memory-intensive applications, basic text processing, single-threaded scripting, and small-scale web serving where high multi-core throughput is not required.
